article.title: Why Growth Among Existing Customers Can Be Hidden by New Customers
article.why: Use cohorts to separate customer development from population-mix change.

paragraphs.en:
A company may report that average spending per customer fell this year. The natural conclusion is that customer value deteriorated. Yet the same data can hide a very different story: existing customers may be spending more while a large number of new, lower-spending customers pull down the overall average.

Suppose a retailer had 100,000 active customers last year, each spending 50,000 yen on average. This year, those retained customers increase their average spending to 55,000 yen. At the same time, the retailer acquires 50,000 new customers who spend only 20,000 yen during their first year. Across all 150,000 customers, average spending becomes about 43,300 yen. The headline average falls even though the original customer base improved.

This is a composition effect. Aggregate metrics combine changes in individual behavior with changes in who is included in the population. When the mix changes substantially, the total average may answer a different question from the one managers intend to ask.

Cohort analysis helps. At minimum, separate retained customers, genuinely new customers, reactivated customers, and customers who churned. For retained customers, compare the same people across both periods. For new customers, evaluate early behavior against appropriate acquisition benchmarks rather than against mature customers who have had years to develop their relationship with the business.

The reverse can also occur. Overall average spending may rise even while retained customers weaken. If many low-value customers leave, the remaining population becomes more concentrated among heavy users. The average increases because of attrition, not because individual customers improved. This is why a rising average should not automatically be celebrated.

Cohorts are also useful for frequency, channel adoption, product breadth, and membership rank. A rise in app usage among all active customers may reflect the acquisition of digitally oriented new customers rather than adoption by existing customers. To measure adoption, follow the same eligible customers over time.

Analysts should define cohort rules carefully. ‘Existing customer’ may mean active in both years, registered before a cutoff date, or observed for a minimum period. Different definitions answer different questions. The report should state the definition and keep it stable across comparisons.

A practical dashboard can show three layers: the total population, fixed or retained cohorts, and entry/exit groups. This makes it possible to reconcile the headline KPI with the underlying movements. If total spend per customer falls 5 percent while retained-customer spend rises 8 percent, the business can see that acquisition mix is diluting the average rather than assuming that loyalty is weakening.

Population growth is often good news, but it changes the denominator. When a business is trying to understand customer development, the most informative comparison is frequently not ‘all customers this year versus all customers last year,’ but ‘the same customers, observed under comparable conditions.’
paragraphs.zh:
整體平均客單下降，不一定代表既有顧客價值惡化。若retained customers平均消費從5萬升到5.5萬，但同時加入大量第一年只消費2萬的新客，overall average仍可能下降。這是composition effect：aggregate metric同時混合了個人行為變化與population成員變化。

應至少拆分retained、new、reactivated與churned cohorts。反過來，若大量低價值客流失，overall average也可能上升，即使既有客其實變弱。App adoption、frequency、product breadth與rank也有同樣問題。Dashboard最好同時呈現total population、fixed/retained cohort與entry/exit groups，並明確定義cohort規則。
paragraphs.ja:
全体平均利用額が下がっても、既存顧客価値が悪化したとは限りません。retained customersの平均が5万円から5.5万円へ伸びても、初年度2万円程度のnew customerが大量に加わればoverall averageは低下します。これはcomposition effectで、aggregate metricに個人行動変化とpopulation構成変化が混在しています。

retained、new、reactivated、churned cohortを分け、同一顧客を比較します。逆に低価値顧客が大量離脱すると、既存顧客が弱くても平均値だけ上がることがあります。App adoptionやfrequencyにも同じ問題があります。total population、fixed cohort、entry/exit groupを併記し、cohort定義を明確にすることが重要です。

vocabulary.usage: The decline may be a composition effect.
New customers can dilute the average.
Reconcile the headline KPI with cohorts.

business.term: The headline decline is mainly a mix effect; retained customers actually grew.
business.explanation: 說明總體KPI與既有客趨勢方向相反。

sources: Cohort analysis; customer retention and composition effects.
